summary: setup.py executes attacker-controlled shell commands from local Xinference registry and exfiltrates output
details: At install time, setup.py queries a local Xinference API at http://127.0.0.1:9997, enumerates model registrations whose names begin with 'xcmd0', base64-decodes the embedded payload, and runs it via subprocess with shell=True. The decoded command is also written to /tmp/kiki_r.sh with mode 0755, persisting an executable copy on the host for later invocation. The command output is then base64url-encoded and smuggled back out by POSTing a sequence of fake 'flexible' model registrations named 'zqx9pNN<chunk>' to the same Xinference endpoint, turning the model registry into a bidirectional covert channel. Any party able to register a model name on the reachable Xinference instance controls code execution on the installer's host and can recover command output through the registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
